papers.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract Semantic task completion video generation evaluates whether generated videos achieve intended outcomes with semantic grounding, supported by a curated dataset and vision-language model-based benchmark.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Semantic Task Completion Video Generation, an outcome-oriented video generation task. Under this formulation, success requires both achievement of the intended outcome and semantic grounding. Semantic grounding characterizes the correspondence between the reference image and the generated outcome in terms of high-level semantics relevant to the task. Evaluation focuses on the generated outcome and requires neither the presentation of a complete sequence of intermediate task steps nor conventional appearance consistency with the reference image. To support systematic evaluation, we construct SemComp-Data, an evaluation dataset covering six domains. Each instance comprises a reference image, a detailed instruction, a brief instruction, and an outcome-centric video clip. A scalable four-stage curation pipeline converts raw videos into standardized SemComp-Data instances. We further introduce SemComp-Bench, an evaluation protocol that uses a vision-language model (VLM) to answer structured binary questions. SemComp-Bench reports the OA Score and the GR Score for Outcome Achievement and Generation Reliability, respectively. Experiments on representative video generation models show that achieving intended outcomes while maintaining task-relevant semantic grounding in reference images remains challenging.
affiliations: University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: От инструкции к результату: семантически обоснованная генерация видео
ru.desc: В работе предлагается новая задача генерации видео с фокусом на семантическое завершение задач, где качество оценивается по достижению намеченного результата и соответствию между исходным изображением и итоговым видео. Авторы создали датасет SemComp-Data, содержащий примеры из шести различных предметных областей с инструкциями и видеороликами, ориентированными на результат. Для оценки качества разработан бенчмарк SemComp-Bench, использующий vision-language модель для проверки семантической корректности через структурированные вопросы. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что существующие модели генерации видео испытывают сложности в одновременном достижении целевого результата и сохранении семантического соответствия задаче.

en.title: Achieving Outcomes with Semantic Grounding in Video Generation
en.desc: This paper presents a new task called Semantic Task Completion Video Generation, which focuses on creating videos that not only achieve specific outcomes but also maintain a connection to the original reference image through semantic grounding. Semantic grounding ensures that the generated video aligns with the high-level meanings of the task, rather than just visual similarities. The authors introduce a dataset called SemComp-Data, which includes various instances of reference images, instructions, and outcome-focused video clips to facilitate evaluation. They also propose SemComp-Bench, a protocol that uses a vision-language model to assess the success of generated videos based on outcome achievement and generation reliability.

zh.title: 语义驱动的视频生成新挑战
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种新的视频生成任务，称为语义任务完成视频生成。该任务的成功不仅要求生成的视频达到预期结果，还需要与参考图像在语义上相对应。为了支持系统评估，研究者构建了一个名为SemComp-Data的数据集，涵盖六个领域，并引入了SemComp-Bench评估协议。实验表明，在保持与参考图像的语义一致性的同时，实现预期结果仍然具有挑战性。

papers.title: SemaPLC: A Project-Grounded, Verification-Gated Agent Harness for PLC Code Generation
papers.abstract: Abstract SemaPLC is a verification-gated agent harness that validates generated PLC logic through external compilation and live runtime execution, achieving higher verified pass rates than baseline methods.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Programmable logic controllers (PLCs) run industrial plants, and large language models can already generate independent program organization units (POUs) for them. Whether such logic integrates into an existing PLC project and then runs correctly has been checked only in limited tests. We present SemaPLC, a project-grounded and verification-gated agent harness assembled from conventional tools but governed by a strict completion rule. Rather than stopping when the model judges its own output adequate, SemaPLC declares a task complete only when logged external checks confirm it. Those checks cover the specification, the compilation, and the behavior on a live runtime. On 117 independent-POU tasks matching existing benchmarks, it attains the highest strict verified pass rate on all seven models (72.6\% mean). On a project-context track of 65 tasks whose generated logic must compile and run inside a real project, it attains the highest mean on integrated compilation, static behavior, and dynamic behavior. Of the three layers, dynamic behavior is the most revealing. We measure it by deploying the generated and the reference logic to a live PLC runtime and comparing their executed traces. All methods fall within 10 static points of one another, whereas dynamic scores separate them sharply, from 22.4 to 31.4 for the baselines against 52.2 for SemaPLC. Overall, our verification-gated harness raises the mean at every layer and most sharply at runtime. Execution, not static scoring, is the faithful test of whether generated control logic actually works. SemaPLC is open-sourced at https://github.com/midea-ai/SemaPLC.

ru.title: Верификация через выполнение: тестирование сгенерированного кода PLC в реальности
ru.desc: SemaPLC — это система проверки для агентов, которые генерируют код для программируемых логических контроллеров (PLC), используемых в промышленности. Система использует внешнюю компиляцию и прямое выполнение на реальном оборудовании для проверки корректности сгенерированного кода, а не полагается на самооценку модели. На наборе из 117 задач система достигла наивысшего показателя успешной верификации (72,6% в среднем) среди всех протестированных LLM. Особенность работы в том, что динамическая проверка во время выполнения на реальном контроллере показывает наиболее точную оценку качества — разница между методами составляет от 22,4 до 52,2%, что значительно превышает различия на этапе статической проверки.

en.title: SemaPLC: Ensuring Reliable PLC Logic Through Rigorous Verification
en.desc: SemaPLC is a verification-gated agent harness designed to validate the logic generated for programmable logic controllers (PLCs) through external compilation and live execution. It ensures that the generated program organization units (POUs) not only meet specifications but also function correctly in real-time environments. By implementing a strict completion rule, SemaPLC only considers a task complete when external checks confirm its correctness, leading to significantly higher verified pass rates compared to traditional methods. The system excels particularly in dynamic behavior evaluation, demonstrating that execution is the true measure of the effectiveness of generated control logic.

zh.title: SemaPLC：提升PLC逻辑验证的利器
zh.desc: SemaPLC 是一个验证门控的代理工具，旨在通过外部编译和实时执行来验证生成的可编程逻辑控制器（PLC）逻辑。与传统方法相比，SemaPLC 在验证通过率上表现更佳，尤其是在动态行为的测试中。该工具不仅在模型自我评估输出时停止，而是要求外部检查确认任务完成。通过对117个独立的POU任务进行测试，SemaPLC 在所有七个模型中达到了最高的严格验证通过率。

papers.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification
papers.abstract: Abstract Compatible open-weight language model checkpoints share detectable weight-space ancestry signals that distinguish true lineage from independent or distilled models without requiring data.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Open-weight language models are fine-tuned, quantized, pruned, and merged, yet their provenance is often undocumented. We study data-free white-box lineage verification: can weights alone reveal whether two compatible model checkpoints share ancestry?   Residual training produces a shared identity-aligned component in branch products, so this structure alone cannot establish ancestry. We remove it and compare checkpoint-specific structure across residual blocks, yielding a symmetric lineage score calibrated against independent checkpoints. On residual-MLP and GPT-2 benchmarks, the score separates fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned, and quantized descendants from independent and distilled models (AUROC=1.0), distinguishing weight ancestry from behavioral similarity. Under function-preserving checkpoint laundering experiments, weight-space baselines lose margin or fail; our score remains unchanged and runs 76x faster than the nearest robust baseline on GPT-2. The projection-pairing signal appears across six language-model families and beyond, and a case study correctly identifies 3 related and 7 unrelated LLaMA-2 public checkpoints. Collectively, these results establish a passive, data-free provenance signal for compatible open-weight language-model checkpoints

ru.title: Безданные отпечатки предков: восстановление родства моделей через анализ весов
ru.desc: В статье предложен метод определения родства между checkpoints языковых моделей на основе анализа весов без использования данных. Авторы обнаружили, что модели, полученные путём fine-tuning, quantization, pruning и merging, оставляют характерные следы в весовом пространстве, которые отличают истинных потомков от независимо обученных или дистиллированных моделей. Разработанный ими симметричный score сравнивает структуру весов в residual блоках, достигая идеального разделения (AUROC=1.0) между потомками и неродственными моделями. Метод остаётся устойчив к попыткам скрыть родство и работает в 76 раз быстрее аналогичных решений на примере GPT-2 и других семейств языковых моделей.

en.title: Uncovering Ancestry in Language Models Using Weights Alone
en.desc: This paper explores how to determine the ancestry of open-weight language models using only their weights, without needing any training data. It introduces a method for lineage verification that distinguishes between models that share a common origin and those that are independently developed. The authors demonstrate that their approach can accurately identify relationships among various model checkpoints, achieving perfect separation between related and unrelated models. Their findings suggest a reliable way to trace the lineage of language models, which is crucial for understanding their development and ensuring transparency in machine learning.

zh.title: 无数据的语言模型血统验证
zh.desc: 这篇论文研究了开放权重语言模型的血统验证问题。作者提出了一种无数据的白盒验证方法，通过分析模型权重来判断两个模型是否有共同的祖先。研究表明，残差训练会产生共享的身份对齐组件，但这不足以确定血统。最终，作者开发的对称血统评分能够有效区分不同来源的模型，且在多个基准测试中表现出色。

papers.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
papers.abstract: Abstract SoftVTBench introduces a synchronized visuo-tactile dataset and deformation-aware benchmark for evaluating physical interaction quality during deformable-object manipulation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Physical interaction quality is central to deformable-object manipulation, yet most benchmarks evaluate task success alone. A policy may complete the task while allowing slip or causing excessive compression. A primary bottleneck is the absence of visuo-tactile datasets that pair policy-visible contact observations with independent physical ground truth over complete tasks. We introduce SoftVTBench, a visuo-tactile dataset for physical-interaction-aware deformable-object manipulation. It contains 4,000 expert demonstrations and more than 50 assets, including volumetric deformable objects and visually matched rigid twins. At 20 Hz, each episode synchronizes multi-view RGB, dual-finger tactile RGB and marker motion, proprioception, language, and binary and continuous gripper actions, alongside evaluator-only finite-element (FEM) states. Building upon this dataset, we establish a closed-loop benchmark that uses fixed object-specific calibration to define the Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR), which counts a rollout as successful only when it completes the task and keeps peak normalized deformation within tolerance. Across Diffusion Policy, π_{0.5}, and FastWAM, all 12 in-distribution configurations contain successful rollouts that violate the deformation tolerance, accounting for 0.7--24% of each configuration's successes. Under distribution shift, visuo-tactile variants achieve higher task success in all six policy--suite comparisons and higher DSR in five, whereas their in-distribution benefits are mixed. These results show that making touch available does not by itself ensure effective multimodal fusion. SoftVTBench therefore provides a common visuo-tactile resource for studying not only whether a policy succeeds, but how it physically interacts with deformable objects and when touch improves that interaction.
affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

ru.title: Оценка качества физического взаимодействия при манипулировании мягкими объектами
ru.desc: Авторы представляют SoftVTBench — набор данных, который синхронизирует визуальные и тактильные наблюдения при манипулировании деформируемыми объектами, содержащий 4000 экспертных демонстраций и более 50 различных объектов. На основе этого датасета они предлагают бенчмарк с метрикой Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR), которая оценивает не только успешное выполнение задачи, но и качество физического взаимодействия, включая избежание чрезмерного сжатия и проскальзывания. Исследование показывает, что даже успешные развертывания политик часто нарушают ограничения на деформацию объектов (от 0,7 до 24% случаев), а наличие тактильной информации не гарантирует эффективное мультимодальное слияние данных. SoftVTBench служит общим ресурсом для изучения того, как именно политики физически взаимодействуют с деформируемыми объектами и когда тактильная обратная связь действительно улучшает результаты.

en.title: Enhancing Deformable Object Manipulation with Visuo-Tactile Insights
en.desc: SoftVTBench is a new dataset designed to improve the evaluation of how well machines manipulate deformable objects by considering both visual and tactile feedback. Traditional benchmarks often only measure whether a task is completed, ignoring the quality of physical interactions like slipping or excessive compression. This dataset includes 4,000 expert demonstrations and various objects, providing synchronized data on visual and tactile inputs, as well as physical states. The study introduces a new metric, the Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR), which assesses not just task completion but also the quality of the manipulation, highlighting the importance of integrating tactile information for better performance.

zh.title: 变形物体操作的新基准：SoftVTBench
zh.desc: SoftVTBench是一个同步的视觉-触觉数据集和变形感知基准，用于评估可变形物体操作过程中的物理交互质量。该数据集包含4000个专家演示和50多个资产，提供多视角RGB图像、双指触觉RGB图像和其他传感器数据。通过建立变形感知成功率（DSR）基准，研究者可以评估操作是否成功以及在操作过程中物体的变形是否在容忍范围内。结果表明，触觉信息的引入并不总能保证有效的多模态融合，SoftVTBench为研究物理交互提供了重要资源。

papers.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
papers.abstract: Abstract SPADE is a self-play reinforcement learning framework where a language model designs adaptive executable training environments and learns to solve them, improving reasoning and tool-use performance through regret-based environment targeting.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Continuous self-improvement requires an ever-expanding pool of self-generated, diverse, adaptive goals. For language agents, existing training environment pools (hand-curated, statically synthesized, or frozen-verifier) keep the goal distribution fixed as the learner scales. We introduce SPADE (Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments), a self-play RL framework in which a single LLM plays two roles: an Environment Designer that writes complete, long-horizon training environments as executable code with an OpenAI Gym-style reset()/step() interface, and a Reasoning Agent that learns to act in them. Each is a stateful, multi-turn environment (state transitions, reward functions, and verification code), so one interface spans reasoning problems and multi-step agentic tool use. The Reasoning Agent's regret is estimated using the gap between its reward with and without privileged hints; in optimizing this regret signal the Environment Designer learns to target environments at the edge of the agent's capabilities while keeping them feasible. Through extensive experimentation, we find several components critical to success: grounding the Environment Designer on documents sampled from a large pretraining corpus, and giving it an accumulated environment memory. Scaling to 30B-parameter models, SPADE improves over the strongest fixed-environment baseline by +5.3 on average across eight held-out math, science, code, and reasoning benchmarks, and lifts the tool-use setting by +5.7 on BFCL-v4 multi-turn and +13.9 on ACEBench-Agent; on the games setting, the margin over the strongest baseline grows with model scale. By making environment design itself a learnable component, SPADE takes a concrete step toward open-ended self-improvement.

ru.title: Модель, которая сама создаёт себе задачи для самосовершенствования
ru.desc: SPADE — это фреймворк обучения с подкреплением, где одна языковая модель играет две роли: создатель окружения, который пишет адаптивные тренировочные задачи как исполняемый код, и агента, который учится их решать. Агент улучшает свои навыки через сигнал сожаления (regret), измеряемый разницей между его производительностью с подсказками и без них, что позволяет создателю окружения генерировать задачи на границе возможностей агента. Система использует память накопленных окружений и документы из корпуса предварительного обучения для более эффективного дизайна задач. Метод показал значительные улучшения на бенчмарках математики, науки, программирования и использования инструментов — на 5-14 процентных пункта выше существующих подходов.

en.title: SPADE: Self-Improving Learning through Adaptive Environment Design
en.desc: SPADE is a novel self-play reinforcement learning framework that enables a language model to create adaptive training environments while simultaneously learning to solve them. It features two main roles: an Environment Designer that generates executable training scenarios and a Reasoning Agent that interacts with these environments. The framework uses a regret-based approach to optimize the learning process, allowing the Environment Designer to create challenges that are just within the agent's capabilities. By leveraging self-generated goals and scaling to large models, SPADE significantly enhances performance in reasoning and tool-use tasks compared to traditional fixed-environment methods.

zh.title: 自我对弈：开启开放式自我改进的新篇章
zh.desc: SPADE是一种自我对弈的强化学习框架，利用语言模型设计自适应的可执行训练环境，并通过基于遗憾的环境目标优化来提高推理和工具使用的表现。该框架中，语言模型同时扮演环境设计者和推理代理的角色，设计出具有多轮状态转移和奖励函数的复杂环境。通过对环境设计的学习，SPADE能够生成多样化的目标，促进自我改进。实验结果表明，SPADE在多个基准测试中显著超越了传统的固定环境基线，展示了其在开放式自我改进方面的潜力。

papers.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract FM-Bench evaluates long-horizon decision-making of LLM agents managing a football club over 20 years, revealing that managerial behavior rather than scale or token spend drives performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Language model agents now execute bounded tasks reliably. Whether they can sustain effective decision-making over long horizons, where actions have cumulative consequences and the environment responds to their choices, remains largely unmeasured. FM-Bench (Football Management Benchmark) measures this. An LLM agent runs a football club for 20 in-game years through 26 tools and roughly 340 to 400 decision stops. It drafts a squad on the same budget as every rival, trades players, negotiates contracts, invests in facilities and youth, sets lineups, and answers to a board that can fire it, while a deterministic engine accumulates every year into one final score with no LLM judge or human rater. The solo track plays each of 15 frontier models against a frozen scripted world, and the Arena places the same models plus a scripted anchor in one shared 20-year world; to our knowledge, the first head-to-head evaluation at this scale. We measure six behavioral capabilities behind the score. Across three seeds, all 15 models complete every horizon while the blind scripted baselines die out in most of theirs, and claude-fable-5 tops the solo board on mean score and the Arena, where the title nonetheless rotates among ten models. Neither scale, price, nor vendor predicts the order; the order settles only late in the horizon, and the best first-play human lands only at the bottom of the model board. What separates the models is managerial behavior rather than computation. Higher-scoring models reduce slow-payoff investment near the end, keep cash invested rather than idle, and open renewals well before the deadline, while token spend predicts nothing. No model learns the market's hidden prices from hundreds of rejected bids, and self-managed memory fails in two opposite modes: an archive that only grows or a plan rewritten every season. Code is available at https://github.com/Analogy-AI/fm-bench.

ru.title: Мастерство управления превосходит размер модели
ru.desc: В статье представлен FM-Bench — бенчмарк для оценки долгосрочного принятия решений агентами на основе LLM, которые управляют футбольным клубом в течение 20 игровых сезонов. Агент взаимодействует с детерминированной средой через 26 инструментов и около 340-400 точек принятия решений, выполняя задачи подобные подбору команды, торговле игроками и управлению инвестициями. Исследование показывает, что среди 15 фронтальных моделей различия в производительности определяются поведенческими стратегиями управления, а не масштабом модели или объемом потраченных токенов. Ключевое открытие состоит в том, что успешные модели демонстрируют специфические поведенческие паттерны: сокращение долгосрочных инвестиций в конце периода, сохранение активов в инвестициях и своевременное возобновление контрактов.

en.title: Managerial Behavior Trumps Scale in Long-Term Decision-Making
en.desc: FM-Bench is a benchmark designed to evaluate the long-term decision-making abilities of large language model (LLM) agents in managing a football club over a span of 20 years. The study reveals that the effectiveness of these agents is influenced more by their managerial behavior than by their computational scale or token expenditure. The benchmark involves various tasks such as player trading, contract negotiations, and strategic investments, with performance measured through cumulative outcomes rather than immediate results. Notably, the findings indicate that successful models prioritize timely investments and proactive management, while traditional metrics like token spend do not correlate with success.

zh.title: 管理行为决定足球俱乐部的成功
zh.desc: FM-Bench是一个评估大型语言模型（LLM）代理在管理足球俱乐部时的长期决策能力的基准测试。研究表明，管理行为比模型的规模或花费的代币更能影响表现。该基准测试通过模拟20年内的决策过程，考察了模型在不同情境下的表现。结果显示，成功的模型在投资和决策时更具前瞻性，而不是单纯依赖计算能力。

papers.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Top-K prompting and plausibility-aware training improve diverse reaction prediction in single-step retrosynthesis, yielding state-of-the-art results on a large verified reaction dataset and motivating ensemble systems.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Single-step retrosynthesis is a central component of computer-aided synthesis planning, yet its intrinsically one-to-many nature is poorly captured by single-answer evaluation and benchmarking protocols. To address this, we introduce Top-K prompting as a robust training and inference paradigm to better capture diverse, plausible reaction predictions. We compile CREED-CCV-2+USPTO-XL, an ultra-large-scale dataset of ~45.6 million verified reactions to train the C3LM (Chemistry Constraint-Consistent Language Model). By integrating fine-tuning with ChemCensor-based and novelty-oriented rewards, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the OOD URSA-expert-2026 benchmark. Further analysis of reaction uniqueness shows that LLMs and conventional models explore complementary reaction spaces, motivating ensemble-based retrosynthesis systems. Overall, our results establish Top-K, plausibility-aware training as a practical new direction for robust future LLM-based synthesis planning.
affiliations: Insilico Medicine AI Limited, Abu Dhabi, UAE
Insilico Medicine Canada Inc., Montreal, Quebec, Canada
Insilico Medicine Hong Kong Ltd., Hong Kong SAR, China

ru.title: Многовариантное предсказание реакций через Top-K промптинг и ансамбльные системы
ru.desc: Статья посвящена улучшению предсказания реакций в одношаговом ретросинтезе с помощью техники Top-K промптинга и обучения с учетом правдоподобия. Авторы создали огромный датасет из 45.6 миллионов верифицированных реакций и обучили языковую модель C3LM, которая достигла лучших результатов на бенчмарке URSA-expert-2026. Анализ показал, что большие языковые модели и традиционные модели исследуют дополняющие друг друга пространства реакций, что мотивирует использование ансамблевых систем. Работа предлагает новый практический подход к обучению LLM-моделей для планирования синтеза на основе оценки плауцибилити предсказанных реакций.

en.title: Enhancing Reaction Diversity with Top-K Prompting in Retrosynthesis
en.desc: This paper presents a new approach called Top-K prompting to improve the prediction of diverse reactions in single-step retrosynthesis, which is important for computer-aided synthesis planning. The authors introduce a large dataset, CREED-CCV-2+USPTO-XL, containing approximately 45.6 million verified reactions to train their model, C3LM. By using a combination of fine-tuning techniques and rewards focused on novelty, the model achieves top performance on established benchmarks. The findings suggest that combining different models can enhance the exploration of reaction possibilities, paving the way for more effective synthesis planning systems.

zh.title: Top-K提示：提升逆合成反应预测的多样性与合理性
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的训练和推理方法，称为Top-K提示，以提高单步逆合成中反应预测的多样性和合理性。通过使用一个包含约4560万条验证反应的超大规模数据集，训练了C3LM模型。该模型结合了基于ChemCensor的奖励和新颖性导向的微调，达到了在OOD URSA-expert-2026基准测试中的最佳性能。研究表明，大型语言模型和传统模型在反应空间的探索上具有互补性，推动了基于集成的逆合成系统的发展。

papers.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
papers.abstract: Abstract Looped language models improve compositional, multi-step tool use through recurrent computation, with adaptive inference balancing accuracy and compute cost.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Looped language models have shown promising results on reasoning benchmarks, yet their potential for agentic tool use remains largely unexplored. We study this question in compositional tool-calling settings, where models must coordinate multiple API calls, maintain intermediate state, and preserve dependencies across tool interactions. We evaluate native and retrofitted looped language models on API-Bank, BFCL, and NESTful, comparing looped and non-looped models trained under matched supervised fine-tuning recipes and varying recurrent depth at inference time. In controlled experiments, recurrent computation generally benefits compositional and dependency-aware tool use, while providing smaller and more model-dependent gains on isolated API invocation. Accuracy on multi-step tool use generally increases with recurrent depth; adaptive inference, however, achieves a more favorable compute-performance trade-off by allocating additional computation only when needed. Our results suggest that looped language models are a promising architecture for agentic systems that require reliable planning, coordination, and execution of compositional tool use workflows.

ru.title: Циклические модели для многошаговой координации инструментов с адаптивными вычислениями
ru.desc: В работе исследуются циклические языковые модели, которые используют рекуррентные вычисления для улучшения композитного использования инструментов через API-вызовы. Авторы оценивают как нативные, так и адаптированные циклические модели на бенчмарках API-Bank, BFCL и NESTful, сравнивая их с обычными моделями при различной глубине рекуррентности. Результаты показывают, что рекуррентные вычисления особенно эффективны для многошаговых задач, требующих координации нескольких вызовов и сохранения зависимостей между ними. Адаптивный вывод позволяет достичь лучшего баланса между точностью и вычислительными затратами, выделяя дополнительные ресурсы только при необходимости.

en.title: Enhancing Tool Use with Looped Language Models
en.desc: This paper explores the effectiveness of looped language models in performing complex tasks that require multiple steps and coordination between different tools. These models utilize recurrent computation to enhance their ability to manage dependencies and maintain state across various API calls. The study evaluates the performance of these models against traditional ones, showing that increased recurrent depth generally improves accuracy in multi-step tasks. Additionally, the introduction of adaptive inference allows for a more efficient balance between computational cost and performance, making looped models suitable for systems that need reliable planning and execution.

zh.title: 循环语言模型：提升工具使用的智能系统
zh.desc: 循环语言模型通过递归计算提高了组合性和多步骤工具使用的能力，同时在准确性和计算成本之间实现了自适应推理的平衡。尽管循环语言模型在推理基准测试中表现良好，但其在自主工具使用方面的潜力仍未得到充分探索。我们在组合工具调用的环境中研究了这一问题，模型需要协调多个API调用，维护中间状态，并保持工具交互之间的依赖关系。实验结果表明，递归计算通常有利于组合和依赖感知的工具使用，同时在单独的API调用中提供的增益较小且依赖于模型。
